title: May Day in Moscow and a lost drosky ride to the theater
summary: Wooding describes the May Day parade and a drosky ride in which neither driver nor bystanders could read the black head placard.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: With a scarf. In those days -- of course Russians have everything now -- but in those days they were very poor. And we have seen them, some people laying in the snow, asleep. But that's all finished. And of course, when I come back and was in -- in '52, in Paris, I saw men sleep in the subway, same way. So that was nothing to brag about, but we had a wonderful time, because the time we were in Russia, at Mayday. And that was something that was good to see, because they had the torch burning. And we were up in the window, we lived in a hotel called the Yanka, Yaka Hotel. And they were bright and begging us to come down and join the parade. But we were supposed to be non-partisan, we were artists. But on the whole, there was quite a lot of illiteracy at the time. I know, once we came to -- I was out shopping one day and we had a theater matinee. Well, I realized that the time was gone, so now I can't speak Russian. I can't tell the man where to go, how to get to the theater. I'm late, you see, so I told him to keep driving, you know?

'cause There was a great sign language, you see. I told him to keep driving until he come to a statue. Of course we had for our placard, we had for our placard, a big black head, you know what I mean?
A big, black head like you see in the carnival or something. And that was saying that this black show was there.

and we were a sensation Well, when he got there, he couldn't read it, and nobody else could read it that we passed. So he's there and he can't read what it is, so he don't know where it is. So, I was in a drosky. About that time a little girl came by and she told him where it was. Now, there must have been eight or ten people out there, but they couldn't read it.
